en: The Path of Discrimination 1,
Great Chapter 1.5.
Discussion on Liberation
1.5.1. Summary: The Previous Introduction.
“Monks, there are these three liberations.”
Which three?
The void liberation, the signless liberation, and the desireless liberation—
these, monks, are the three liberations.
Furthermore, there are sixty-eight liberations:
the void liberation, the signless liberation, the desireless liberation;
the liberation emerging from the internal, the liberation emerging from the external, the liberation emerging from both;
There are four liberations emerging from within; four liberations emerging from without; and four liberations emerging from both.

There are four liberations in conformity with those emerging from within; four liberations in conformity with those emerging from without; and four liberations in conformity with those emerging from both.

There are four liberations through the subsiding of emergence from within; four liberations through the subsiding of emergence from without; and four liberations through the subsiding of emergence from both.
The liberation consisting in "one possessing form sees forms"; the liberation consisting in "not perceiving forms internally, one sees forms externally";

the liberation consisting in "being intent upon the beautiful"; the attainment of the base of infinite space as liberation; the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness as liberation; the attainment of the base of nothingness as liberation;
the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception as liberation; and the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling as liberation.
liberation by occasion, liberation not by occasion; occasional liberation, non-occasional liberation;
shaken liberation, unshaken liberation.
mundane liberation, supramundane liberation;
liberation with taints, liberation without taints;
carnal liberation, non-carnal liberation.
Liberation that is unworldly and more unworldly than the unworldly; directed liberation; undirected liberation; liberation through the subsiding of the directed;
bound liberation; liberated-from-bonds liberation;
unity liberation; diversity liberation; perception liberation; and knowledge liberation.
The liberation that is cool, the liberation of meditative absorption, and the liberation of the mind through non-clinging.
[75] 1.5.2. Exposition:
What is the liberation through emptiness?
Here, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, reflects thus:
"This is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.
He does not form a fixed attachment there.
The void liberation.
This is the void liberation.
What is the signless liberation?
Here, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, reflects thus:
"This is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.
He does not fixate upon a sign therein.
The signless liberation.
This is the signless liberation.
What is the desireless liberation?
Here, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, reflects thus:
"This is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.
He forms no aspiration for that.
The wishless liberation.
This is the wishless liberation.
What is the liberation emerging from the internal?
The four jhānas—
this is the liberation emerging from within.
What is the liberation emerging from without?
The four formless attainments—
this is the liberation emerging externally.
What is the liberation emerging from both sides?
The four noble paths—
this is liberation by emergence from both sides.
What are the four liberations that emerge internally?
The first jhāna emerges from the hindrances;
the second jhāna emerges from applied and sustained thought;
the third jhāna emerges from rapture.
The fourth jhāna emerges from pleasure and pain.
These are the four liberations that emerge internally.
What are the four liberations that emerge externally?
The attainment of the base of infinite space emerges from the perception of form, the perception of resistance, and the perception of diversity.
The attainment of the base of infinite consciousness emerges from the perception of the base of infinite space.
The attainment of the base of nothingness emerges from the perception of the base of infinite consciousness.
The attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception emerges from the perception of the base of nothingness.
These are the four liberations that emerge externally.
What are the four liberations that emerge from both sides?

The path of stream-entry emerges from personality-belief, doubt, and adherence to rules and observances; it emerges from the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to doubt; it emerges from the defilements that follow upon them and from the aggregates; and it emerges from all external signs.
The path of once-returning emerges from the gross fetters of sensual lust and ill will; it emerges from the gross underlying tendencies to sensual lust and ill will;
it emerges from the defilements that follow upon them and from the aggregates; and it emerges from the external...
And he emerges from all signs.

The path of non-returning emerges from the secondary fetters of sensual desire and aversion, from the secondary underlying tendencies of sensual desire and aversion, and it emerges from the defilements that follow those [fetters] as well as from the aggregates; and externally...
And it emerges from all signs.

The path of arahantship emerges from attachment to the fine-material realm, attachment to the immaterial realm, conceit, restlessness, ignorance, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to attachment to existence, and the underlying tendency to ignorance;
it emerges from the defilements that follow upon those [tendencies] and from the aggregates; and externally as well.
One emerges from all signs.
These are the four liberations that emerge from both sides.
What are the four liberations that are in conformity with those that emerge internally?
For the sake of attaining the first jhāna, there is applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and one-pointedness of mind;
for the sake of attaining the second jhāna … pe … for the sake of attaining the third jhāna … pe … for the sake of attaining the fourth jhāna,
there is applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and one-pointedness of mind.
These are the four liberations that are in conformity with emerging from within.
What are the four liberations that are in conformity with emerging from without? They are:

the applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind for the purpose of attaining the base of infinite space; [and likewise] for the base of infinite consciousness... [etc.]

The applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and one-pointedness of mind directed toward the attainment of the base of nothingness …pe… the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception for the purpose of its acquisition—
these are the four liberations in conformity with emergence from the external.
What are the four liberations that are in conformity with emergence from both sides? They are:
the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self for the sake of attaining the path of stream-entry;
[and] for the sake of attaining the path of once-returning... [and so on].

The contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self for the sake of attaining the path of non-returning …pe… and for the sake of attaining the path of arahantship—
these are the four liberations in conformity with emergence from both sides.
What are the four liberations that are the subsiding of emergence from the internal?
They are the attainment or the fruition of the first jhāna;
of the second jhāna … pe … of the third jhāna … pe …
The attainment of the fourth jhāna or its fruition—
these are the four liberations that are the subsiding of emergence from within.
What are the four liberations that are the subsiding of emergence from without?

The attainment of the base of infinite space, or its result; the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness …pe… the attainment of the base of nothingness …pe… the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, or its result.
These four liberations are the subsiding of emergence from the external.
What are the four liberations that are the subsiding of emergence from both sides?

They are: the fruit of stream-entry for the path of stream-entry; the fruit of once-returning for the path of once-returning; the fruit of non-returning for the path of non-returning; and the fruit of arahantship for the path of arahantship.
These four liberations are the subsiding of emergence from both sides.
How is it that "one possessing form sees forms"? This is liberation.
Here, a certain person attends to a blue sign internally within himself and acquires the perception of blue.
Thus he makes that sign well-grasped, well-retained, and well-established.
Having made that sign well-grasped, having retained it well, and having established it well, he directs his mind toward an external blue sign and acquires the perception of blue.
He makes that sign well-grasped, well-retained, and well-established.
Thus, having correctly grasped that sign, having reflected upon it, and having established it well, he pursues it, develops it, and cultivates it frequently.
It occurs to him:
"Both internally and externally, this is form"; thus, he perceives form.
Here, someone attends to an internal personal sign of yellow ... pe ...
a sign of red ... pe ...
a sign of white, and he acquires the perception of white.
Thus he makes that sign well-grasped, well-retained, and well-established.
Having made that sign well-grasped, having retained it well, and having established it well, he directs his mind toward an external white sign and acquires the perception of white.
He makes that sign well-grasped, well-retained, and well-established.
Thus, having well grasped that sign, having well attended to it after attending to it, and having well established it after establishing it, he pursues it, develops it, and cultivates it frequently.
It occurs to him:
"Both internally and externally, this is form"; thus, he perceives form.
"Thus, possessing form, one sees forms"—
this is a liberation.
How is it that "perceiving the formless internally, one sees forms externally"— this is a liberation?
In this case, someone does not attend to a blue sign internally within themselves and does not acquire the perception of blue;
however, they direct the mind toward a blue sign externally and acquires the perception of blue.
They grasp that sign well, retain it well, and establish it firmly.
Thus, having well-grasped that sign, having well-borne it by bearing it in mind, and having well-established it by establishing it, he pursues, develops, and cultivates it repeatedly.
It occurs to him:
"Internally there is no form; externally this is form," and he perceives form.
Here, someone does not attend to the sign of yellow internally within themselves, nor does he attain the perception of yellow;
[likewise] the sign of red...
the sign of white... he does not attend to it, nor does he attain the perception of white.
He directs his mind toward an external white sign and acquires the perception of white.
He grasps that sign well, retains it well, and establishes it firmly.
Having grasped that sign well, retained it well, and established it firmly, he pursues it, develops it, and cultivates it repeatedly.
It occurs to him:
"There is no form internally, but there is this form externally";
thus he perceives form. In this way, one who does not perceive form internally sees forms externally.
Liberation.
How is it that one is resolved upon the beautiful? This is liberation.
Here, a bhikkhu dwells having pervaded one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, and likewise the second, the third, and the fourth.

In the same way the third [direction], in the same way the fourth. Thus, above, below, across, everywhere, and to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness—vast, exalted, immeasurable, free from enmity, and free from ill will.
Because loving-kindness has been developed, beings become free from repulsion.
With a mind accompanied by compassion … [as before] … through the cultivation of compassion, beings become free from repulsiveness.
With a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy … [as before] …
Because sympathetic joy has been cultivated, beings become non-repulsive.
With a mind accompanied by equanimity, he dwells pervading one direction … [as before] … because equanimity has been cultivated, beings become non-repulsive.
Thus, being resolved upon the beautiful itself—
this is liberation.
What is the liberation of the attainment of the base of infinite space?

Here, a bhikkhu, with the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, and with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, thinking "space is infinite," enters and dwells in the base of infinite space—
this is the liberation that is the attainment of the base of infinite space.
What is the liberation that is the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness?
Here, a bhikkhu, by completely transcending the base of infinite space, thinking "consciousness is infinite," enters and dwells in the base of infinite consciousness—
this is the liberation that is the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness.
What is the liberation that is the attainment of the base of nothingness?
Here, a bhikkhu, by completely transcending the base of infinite consciousness, thinking "there is nothing," enters and dwells in the base of nothingness—
this is the liberation that is the attainment of the base of nothingness.
What is the liberation that is the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception?
Here, a bhikkhu, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, enters and dwells in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—
this is the liberation consisting in the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
What is the liberation consisting in the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling?
Here, a bhikkhu, by completely transcending the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, enters and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling—
this is the liberation of the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.
What is temporary liberation?
The four jhānas and the four formless attainments—
this is liberation by occasion.
What is liberation not by occasion?
The four noble paths, the four fruits of recluseship, and Nibbāna—
this is liberation not dependent on occasion. What is liberation dependent on occasion?
The four jhānas and the four formless attainments—
this is liberation by occasion.
What is liberation not by occasion?
The four noble paths, the four fruits of recluseship, and Nibbāna—
this is the non-temporary liberation.
What is the shakable liberation?
The four jhānas and the four formless attainments—
this is the shakable liberation.
What is the unshakable liberation?
The four noble paths, the four fruits of recluseship, and Nibbāna—
this is the unshakable liberation.
What is mundane liberation?
The four jhānas and the four formless attainments—
this is mundane liberation.
What is supramundane liberation?
The four noble paths, the four fruits of recluseship, and Nibbāna—
this is supramundane liberation.
What is mundane liberation?
The four jhānas and the four formless attainments—
this is liberation with taints.
What is liberation without taints?
The four noble paths, the four fruits of recluseship, and Nibbāna—
this is the untainted liberation.
What is the carnal liberation?
Liberation associated with form—
this is liberation that is carnal.
What is liberation that is spiritual?
The liberation associated with the formless—
this is the unworldly liberation.
What is the liberation that is even more unworldly than the unworldly?
The four noble paths, the four fruits of asceticism, and Nibbāna—
this is the liberation that is more unworldly than the unworldly.
What is the directed liberation?
The four jhānas and the four formless attainments—
this is the directed liberation.
What is the undirected liberation?
The four noble paths, the four fruits of asceticism, and Nibbāna—
this is the wishless liberation. What is the liberation by the subsiding of the directed?
The acquisition of the first jhāna or its result, ... pe ...
the acquisition of the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception or its result—this is liberation as the subsiding of the directed.
What is the liberation associated with perception?
The four jhānas and the four formless attainments—
this is the liberation associated with perception.
What is the liberation that is detached?
The four noble paths, the four fruits of recluseship, and Nibbāna—
this is the liberation that is detached.
What is the liberation of unity?
The four noble paths, the four fruits of asceticism, and Nibbāna—
this is the liberation of unity.
What is the liberation of diversity?
The four jhānas and the four formless attainments—
this is the liberation of diversity.
What is liberation by perception (*saññāvimokkha*)?

There may be one liberation by perception that becomes ten liberations by perception, and ten liberations by perception that become one liberation by perception, according to the basis and by way of enumeration. How may this be so?
Knowledge of contemplation of impermanence is liberation from perception as permanent;
thus it is liberation by perception. Knowledge of contemplation of suffering is liberation from perception as pleasant; thus it is liberation by perception.
Liberation from perception:
the knowledge of contemplation of non-self is liberated from the perception of a self; thus it is liberation from perception.
Knowledge of contemplation of disenchantment is liberation from perception through delight; thus it is liberation from perception.
Knowledge of contemplation of fading away is liberation from perception through lust; thus it is liberation from perception.
Liberation from perception.
Knowledge of contemplation of cessation is liberation from perception by way of its arising; thus it is "liberation from perception."
The knowledge of contemplation of relinquishment is liberation from perception because it is released from grasping; thus, it is liberation from perception.
The knowledge of contemplation of the signless is liberation from perception because it is released from signs.
Liberation from perception:
the knowledge of contemplation of the wishless is liberated from the perception of wishing; thus it is liberation from perception.
The knowledge of contemplation of emptiness is liberated from perception by way of misapprehension; thus it is the liberation from perception.

In this way, one liberation from perception may become ten liberations from perception, and ten liberations from perception may become one liberation from perception, according to the basis and by way of a figurative expression.
Knowledge of contemplating impermanence in form is liberation from perception as permanence;
thus it is liberation by perception….
Knowledge of contemplating voidness in form is liberation from perception as misinterpretation; thus it is liberation by perception.
The liberation through perception.

Thus, there may be one liberation through perception that becomes ten liberations through perception, and ten liberations through perception that become one liberation through perception, by way of the basis and by way of method.
[The same applies to] feeling... and so forth.
In perception … in volitional formations … in consciousness …
Knowledge of the contemplation of impermanence in the eye …pe… in aging-and-death is liberated from the perception of permanence;
this is liberation by means of perception …pe…
The knowledge of contemplation of emptiness regarding aging-and-death is liberated from perception due to its adherence; thus it is "liberation by perception.
It may be so: one liberation by perception becomes ten liberations by perception, and ten liberations by perception become one liberation by perception, according to the basis and by way of method.
This is liberation by perception.
What is liberation by knowledge?

There may be one liberation by knowledge that becomes ten liberations by knowledge; there may be ten liberations by knowledge that become one liberation by knowledge, according to the basis and by way of method.
And how would it be so?
The contemplation of impermanence is knowledge as it really is; it is liberation through knowledge because it is released from delusion regarding permanence and from ignorance.
This is liberation through knowledge.
The knowledge that contemplates suffering as it really is is liberated from delusion and ignorance regarding pleasure; thus it is "liberation through knowledge.
The knowledge that contemplates non-self as it really is is liberated from delusion and ignorance regarding self; thus it is [liberation through knowledge].
Liberation through knowledge:
through the contemplation of disenchantment, one is liberated from delight, delusion, and ignorance by means of knowledge as it really is—
this is liberation through knowledge.
The knowledge of contemplating dispassion as it really is is the liberation through knowledge, in that it is liberated from lust, delusion, and ignorance.
The knowledge of contemplating cessation as it really is is [the liberation through knowledge], in that it is liberated from the delusion and ignorance regarding origination.
Liberation through knowledge:
the knowledge that contemplates relinquishment as it truly is is liberated from grasping, delusion, and ignorance; thus it is liberation through knowledge.
The knowledge of seeing things as they truly are through the contemplation of the signless is liberation by knowledge, in that it is liberated from delusion and ignorance regarding signs.
The knowledge of seeing things as they truly are through the contemplation of the desireless is liberation by knowledge, in that it is liberated from delusion and ignorance regarding desire.
Liberation through knowledge:
the contemplation of emptiness is "liberation through knowledge" because it liberates from misapprehension, delusion, and ignorance regarding things as they truly are.

Thus, by way of the basis and by way of a figurative expression, one liberation through knowledge becomes ten liberations through knowledge, and ten liberations through knowledge become one liberation through knowledge.
The knowledge that contemplates impermanence in form as it really is is a liberation through knowledge because it is liberated from delusion regarding permanence and from ignorance. …pe…
The knowledge that sees emptiness in form as it really is is liberated from misapprehension, delusion, and ignorance;
thus it is "liberation by knowledge.
In this way, one liberation by knowledge may become ten liberations by knowledge, and ten liberations by knowledge may become one liberation by knowledge, according to the basis and by way of method.
In feeling … perception … mental formations …
In consciousness … in the eye … [and so on] … in aging-and-death,
the knowledge that is the contemplation of impermanence as it really is is liberated from delusion regarding permanence and from ignorance.

Liberation through knowledge …pe… the knowledge of things as they truly are through the contemplation of emptiness regarding aging-and-death: it is liberated from misapprehension, delusion, and ignorance—
this is liberation through knowledge.

Thus, one liberation through knowledge becomes ten liberations through knowledge, and ten liberations through knowledge become one liberation through knowledge, by way of the basis and by way of method—
this is liberation through knowledge.
What is the liberation of coolness?
One liberation by coolness may become ten liberations by coolness, and ten liberations by coolness may become one liberation by coolness, according to the basis and by way of enumeration.
And how might this be?

Contemplation of impermanence is the unsurpassed knowledge of the state of coolness; it is liberated from the burning, the fever, the distress, and the anguish of [perceiving things as] permanent. Thus it may be.
The liberation of coolness.
Contemplation of suffering is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; because it is liberated from pleasure, from burning, fever, and distress, it is called the liberation of coolness.
The contemplation of non-self is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; because it is liberated from the burning, fever, and distress of selfhood, it is the liberation of coolness.
The contemplation of disenchantment is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; because it is liberated from the burning, fever, and distress of delight, [it is the liberation of coolness].
The liberation of coolness (*sītisiyāvimokkho*).

The contemplation of dispassion (*virāgānupassanā*) is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; because it is liberated from passion, from burning, fever, and distress, it is called the liberation of coolness.
Contemplation of cessation is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; because it is liberated from the fever, burning, and distress of origination, it is the liberation of "becoming cool.
Contemplation of relinquishment is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; because it is liberated from the fever, burning, and distress of grasping, [it is the liberation of "becoming cool"].
The liberation of coolness:
the contemplation of the signless is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; because it is liberated from the fever, the burning, and the distress of signs, it is called the liberation of coolness.
The contemplation of the wishless is the knowledge of supreme coolness; because it is liberated from the fever, burning, and distress of wishing, it is the liberation of coolness.
The contemplation of emptiness is the knowledge of supreme coolness; because it is liberated from the fever, burning, and distress of misapprehension, it is [the liberation of coolness].
The liberation of coolness.
Thus, by way of the basis and by way of enumeration, one liberation of coolness becomes ten liberations of coolness, and ten liberations of coolness become one liberation of coolness.
Contemplation of impermanence in regard to form is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; it is liberated from the burning, fever, and distress of regarding things as permanent.
The liberation of coolness:

… [as before] … the contemplation of emptiness regarding forms is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; because it is liberated from the burning, fever, and distress of clinging, it is called the liberation of coolness.

Thus, one liberation characterized by coolness may become ten liberations characterized by coolness, and ten liberations characterized by coolness may become one liberation characterized by coolness, according to the basis and by way of enumeration.
[The same applies] to feeling ... pe ...
to perception ...
In volitional formations … in consciousness … in the eye … [and so on] … up to … [the six sense bases] … in aging-and-death.

The contemplation of impermanence in aging and death is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; it is liberated from the fever, burning, and distress of [viewing things as] permanent—thus it is the liberation of coolness.

… The contemplation of emptiness in aging and death is the unsurpassed knowledge of coolness; it is liberated from the fever, burning, and distress of [mental] fixation—thus it is the liberation of coolness.
The liberation that is cool. Thus,
one liberation that is cool becomes ten liberations that are cool, and ten liberations that are cool become one liberation that is cool, by way of the basis and by way of enumeration—
this is the liberation that is cool.
What is liberation through meditation?
It is called "meditation" (jhāna) because it meditates upon renunciation;
it is called "meditation" because it consumes sensual desire.
"Liberated while meditating" is liberation through jhāna.
"Causing [the defilements] to burn away while meditating" is liberation through jhāna.
"They meditate" refers to the mental states (dhammas).
It burns away—the defilements.
Because it knows both what has been burned and what is being burned, it is "liberation through meditation" (jhānavimokkha).
Non-ill will meditates—it is thus "meditation" (jhāna).
It consumes ill will, thus it is *jhāna*.
Being liberated while meditating (*jhāyanto*) is *jhāna-vimokkha*.
Being liberated while consuming [defilements] is *jhāna-vimokkha*.
They meditate upon it—thus, "states" (dhammā).
It consumes the defilements—thus, "it consumes" (jhāpeti).
One knows both what has been meditated upon and what has been consumed—thus, "liberation through meditation" (jhānavimokkha).
Perception of light meditates,
thus it is jhāna. It burns away sloth and torpor,
thus it is jhāna … [and so on] … Non-distraction meditates, thus it is jhāna.
It burns away restlessness, thus it is *jhāna*.
It burns away the discernment of phenomena, thus it is *jhāna*.
It burns away doubt, thus it is *jhāna*.
Knowledge meditates, thus it is *jhāna*.
It consumes ignorance, thus it is *jhāna*.
It meditates on gladness, thus it is *jhāna*.
It burns away aversion, thus it is *jhāna*.
It meditates with the first *jhāna*, thus it is *jhāna*.
It burns away the hindrances, thus it is *jhāna* ... [and so on] ...
The path to arahantship meditates, thus it is jhāna.
It burns up all defilements, thus it is jhāna.
While meditating, one is liberated, thus it is jhāna-vimokkha.
"By burning, one is liberated"—this is liberation through jhāna.
"They burn"—this refers to phenomena (dhammas).
"It burns"—this refers to the defilements (kilesas).
Because one knows while meditating and while incinerating, it is called "liberation through meditation" (*jhāna-vimokkha*); this is liberation through meditation.
What is liberation of the mind through non-clinging (*anupādā-citta-vimokkha*)?

There may be one liberation of the mind through non-clinging that becomes ten liberations of the mind through non-clinging; and ten liberations of the mind through non-clinging may become one liberation of the mind through non-clinging, according to the basis and by way of method.
And how would it be so?
The knowledge of the contemplation of impermanence is liberated from grasping at the permanent;
thus, there is the liberation of a mind free from grasping.
The knowledge of contemplation of suffering is liberated from clinging to [it] as pleasant;
thus, there is the liberation of the mind through non-clinging.
The knowledge of contemplation of non-self is liberated from clinging to [it] as self; thus...
The liberation of the mind through non-clinging:
the knowledge of contemplation of disenchantment is liberated from clinging to delight;
thus it is the liberation of the mind through non-clinging.
The knowledge of contemplation of dispassion is the liberation of the non-clinging mind because it is released from clinging through lust.
The knowledge of contemplation of cessation is [the liberation] because it is released from clinging through origination.
The liberation of the mind through non-clinging:
because the knowledge that contemplates relinquishment is liberated from grasping and clinging,
it is called "the liberation of the mind through non-clinging."
The knowledge of contemplation of the signless is the liberation of the mind through non-clinging, in that it is freed from clinging to signs.
The knowledge of contemplation of the desireless is [the liberation of the mind through non-clinging], in that it is freed from clinging to desire.
The liberation of the mind through non-clinging:
the knowledge of contemplation of emptiness is liberated from clinging due to misapprehension;
thus, it is the liberation of the mind through non-clinging.

Thus, one liberation of the mind through non-clinging becomes ten liberations of the mind through non-clinging, and ten liberations of the mind through non-clinging become one liberation of the mind through non-clinging, by way of their basis and by way of method.
Knowledge of the contemplation of impermanence in material form is liberated from clinging to it as permanent;
thus it is a liberation of the mind through non-clinging ... [and so on] ...
"Knowledge of contemplation of emptiness regarding form is liberated from adherence and clinging"—this is liberation of mind through non-clinging.

Thus, what may be one liberation of mind through non-clinging becomes ten liberations of mind through non-clinging; and the ten liberations of mind through non-clinging become one liberation of mind through non-clinging by way of the basis and by way of method.
In feeling …pe… in perception … in volitional formations …
Knowledge of the contemplation of impermanence in consciousness … in the eye … [and so on] … in aging-and-death, is liberated from grasping after what is permanent— thus it is said.
The liberation of the non-clinging mind ... [as before] ...
the knowledge of contemplating emptiness regarding aging and death is liberated from clinging through its adherence;
thus it is the liberation of the non-clinging mind.

Thus, one liberation of the mind through non-clinging becomes ten liberations of the mind through non-clinging, and ten liberations of the mind through non-clinging become one liberation of the mind through non-clinging, by way of their basis and by way of method.
Through how many kinds of clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of impermanence liberated?
Through how many kinds of clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of suffering liberated?
From how many kinds of clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of non-self liberated?
The knowledge of contemplation of disenchantment … the knowledge of contemplation of fading away … [is liberated from them].
Knowledge of contemplation of cessation… knowledge of contemplation of relinquishment… knowledge of contemplation of the signless…
How many kinds of clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of the wishless liberated from? How many kinds of clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of emptiness liberated from?
The knowledge of contemplation of impermanence is liberated from three kinds of clinging.
Knowledge of contemplation of suffering is liberated from one kind of clinging;
knowledge of contemplation of non-self is liberated from three kinds of clinging;
knowledge of contemplation of disenchantment is liberated from one kind of clinging.
The knowledge of contemplation of dispassion is liberated from one type of clinging.
The knowledge of contemplation of cessation is liberated from four types of clinging.
The knowledge of contemplation of relinquishment is liberated from four types of clinging.
The knowledge of contemplation of the signless is liberated from three kinds of clinging.
The knowledge of contemplation of the desireless is liberated from one kind of clinging.
The knowledge of contemplation of emptiness is liberated from three kinds of clinging.
From which three kinds of clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of impermanence liberated?
From clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self—
the knowledge of contemplation of impermanence is liberated from these three kinds of clinging.
From which single clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of suffering liberated?
From clinging to sensual pleasures—
the knowledge of contemplation of suffering is liberated from this one clinging.
From which three kinds of clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of non-self liberated?
From clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self—
the knowledge of contemplation of non-self is liberated from these three kinds of clinging.
What single clinging is knowledge of contemplation of disenchantment liberated from?
It is clinging to sensual pleasures—
knowledge of contemplation of disenchantment is liberated from this one clinging.
What is the knowledge of contemplation of dispassion that is liberated from one kind of clinging?
From clinging to sensual pleasures—
this knowledge of contemplation of dispassion is liberated from one kind of clinging.
From which four kinds of clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of cessation liberated?
From clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self—
the knowledge of contemplation of cessation is liberated from these four kinds of clinging.
From which four kinds of clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of relinquishment liberated?
From clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self—
the knowledge of contemplation of relinquishment is liberated from these four kinds of clinging.
From which three kinds of clinging is the knowledge of the contemplation of the signless liberated?
From clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self—
the knowledge of the contemplation of the signless is liberated from these three kinds of clinging.
What single clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of the desireless liberated from?
It is clinging to sense pleasures—
from this single clinging, the knowledge of contemplation of the desireless is liberated.
From which three kinds of clinging is the knowledge of contemplation of emptiness liberated?
From clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self—
the knowledge of contemplation of emptiness is liberated from these three kinds of clinging.
The knowledge of contemplating impermanence, the knowledge of contemplating non-self, the knowledge of contemplating the signless, and the knowledge of contemplating emptiness—
these four knowledges are liberated from three kinds of clinging:
clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self.
The knowledge of contemplation of suffering, the knowledge of contemplation of disenchantment, the knowledge of contemplation of dispassion, and the knowledge of contemplation of the wishless—
these four knowledges are liberated from a single clinging:
clinging to sensual pleasures.
The knowledge that contemplates cessation and the knowledge that contemplates relinquishment—
these two knowledges are liberated from the four kinds of clinging:
clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self.
This is the liberation of the mind through non-clinging.
This concludes the first section of the discourse on liberation.
Furthermore, there are these three gateways to liberation that lead to the transcendence of the world.
Through the contemplation of all formations as limited and circumscribed, there is the leaping of the mind into the signless element;
through the inciting of the mind toward all formations, there is the leaping of the mind into the desireless element;
and through the contemplation of all phenomena as other, there is the leaping of the mind into the void element.
These three gateways to liberation lead to the escape from the world.
When one attends to things as impermanent, how do formations appear?
When one attends to them as suffering, how do formations appear?
When one attends to formations as non-self, how do they appear?

When attending to them as impermanent, formations appear as subject to destruction; when attending to them as suffering, formations appear as fearful; when attending to them as non-self, formations appear as empty.
When attending to them as impermanent, what kind of mind becomes predominant?
When attending to [the object] as suffering, what kind of mind is predominant?
When attending to it as non-self, what kind of mind is predominant?
When attending to it as impermanent, the mind is predominantly characterized by resolution.
When attending to [the object] as suffering, the mind becomes abundant in tranquility.
When attending to it as non-self, the mind becomes abundant in equanimity.
When attending to it as impermanent, what faculty does one who is abundant in resolve acquire?
When attending to [the object] as suffering, one who abounds in tranquility acquires which faculty?
When attending to it as non-self, one who abounds in wisdom acquires which faculty?
When attending to it as impermanent, one who abounds in resolve acquires the faculty of faith.
One who attends to [the object] as suffering, being abundant in tranquility, acquires the faculty of concentration.
One who attends to it as non-self, being abundant in wisdom, acquires the faculty of wisdom.
For one who attends to it as impermanent and is abundant in resolve, which faculty becomes predominant in cultivation?
Which faculties are its concomitants, are co-nascent conditions, are mutual conditions, are support conditions, and are association conditions;
how do they have a single flavor; in what sense is it "development" (bhāvanā); and who develops it?
For one who attends to [the body] as suffering and for whom tranquility is predominant, which faculty becomes dominant through development?
Which faculties are its consequents, its co-nascence conditions, its mutuality conditions, its support conditions, and its association conditions?
Are they of a single flavor? In what sense is there "development" (*bhāvanā*), and who develops?
For one who attends to [the aggregates] as non-self and for whom wisdom (*vedā*) is predominant, which faculty becomes dominant? Which faculties are there in development?
They are its consequents; they are co-nascence conditions; they are mutuality conditions; they are support conditions;
they are association conditions; they have a single flavor. In what sense is it "development" (bhāvanā)? Who develops it?
For one who attends to [the object] as impermanent and who abounds in resolution, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.

Through development, the four faculties follow along with it, they are co-nascent conditions, they are mutual conditions, they are support conditions, they are associated conditions, and they have a single function.
In the sense of having a single function, there is development.
One who has practiced rightly develops them.
For one who has entered upon a wrong course, there is no development of the faculties.
For one who attends to [the body] as suffering and abounds in tranquility, the faculty of concentration becomes predominant.
Through development, the four faculties follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, associated conditions, and they have a single flavor.
Development is in the sense of having a single flavor.
One who is practicing rightly develops [the faculties];
for one who is practicing wrongly, there is no development of the faculties.
For one who attends to [the aggregates] as not-self and is abundant in wisdom, the faculty of wisdom is predominant.
In the course of development, the four faculties follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, associated conditions, and they have a single flavor.
Development is so called in the sense of having a single flavor.
One who has practiced rightly develops [the faculties];
for one who has practiced wrongly, there is no development of the faculties.
When one attends to impermanence and is abundant in resolution, which faculty becomes predominant?
In the development [of the path], which faculties follow along with it, are co-nascent conditions, are mutual conditions, are support conditions, and are associated conditions?
At the time of penetration, which faculty is predominant?
For the sake of penetration, which faculties follow along with it, are co-nascent conditions, are mutual conditions, are support conditions, are associated conditions, and are of a single flavor?
In what sense is it "development"?
In what sense is it "penetration"?
For one who attends to [the body] as suffering and abounds in tranquility, which faculty becomes predominant?
In the development [of the path], which faculties follow along with it, are co-nascent conditions, are mutual conditions, are support conditions, and are associated conditions?
At the time of penetration, which faculty is predominant?
For the sake of penetration, which faculties follow along with it, are co-nascent conditions, are mutual conditions, are support conditions, are associated conditions, and are of a single flavor?
In what sense is there "development"?
In what sense is there "penetration"?
For one who attends to [the aggregates] as non-self and is abundant in wisdom, which faculty is predominant?
In the development [of the path], which faculties follow along with it, are co-nascent conditions, are mutual conditions, are support conditions, and are associated conditions?
At the time of penetration, which faculty is predominant?
For the sake of penetration, which faculties follow along with it, are co-nascent conditions, are mutual conditions, are support conditions, are associated conditions, and are of a single flavor?
In what sense is there "development"?
In what sense is there "penetration"?
For one who attends to [the object] as impermanent and for whom resolution is predominant, the faculty of faith becomes dominant.
In the stage of development (bhāvanā), the four faculties follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions.
At the time of penetration (paṭivedha), the faculty of wisdom (paññindriya) is predominant.

For the sake of penetration, the four faculties follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions, and they have a single flavor (ekarasa).
Development is in the sense of a single flavor;
penetration is in the sense of seeing.
Thus, while penetrating, one develops; while developing, one penetrates.
For one who attends to [the body] as suffering and possesses abundant tranquility, the faculty of concentration is predominant.
During the stage of development, the four faculties follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions.
At the time of penetration, the faculty of wisdom is predominant.

For the sake of penetration, the four faculties follow upon that [insight]; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions; they have a single flavor.
In the sense of having a single flavor, there is development (bhāvanā);
in the sense of seeing, there is penetration (paṭivedha).
Thus, while penetrating, one develops; while developing, one penetrates.
For one who attends to [the aggregates] as non-self and possesses abundant wisdom, the faculty of wisdom is predominant.
Through development, the other four faculties follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions.
At the time of penetration as well, the faculty of wisdom is predominant.
For the sake of penetration, the other four faculties follow it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, associated conditions, and they have a single function.
In the sense of having a single function, there is development (bhāvanā).
Penetration is in the sense of seeing.
One who penetrates thus also develops [the path], and one who develops it also penetrates.
When attending to [the object] as impermanent, which faculty becomes predominant?
Through the predominance of which faculty does one become "liberated by faith"?
When attending to [the aggregates] as suffering, which faculty becomes predominant?
Through the predominance of which faculty does one become a "body-witness"?
When one attends to [the aggregates] as non-self, which faculty becomes predominant?
Through the predominance of which faculty does one become one who has attained vision?
When attending to them as impermanent, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the faculty of faith, one is "liberated by faith.
When attending to [the body] as suffering, the faculty of concentration becomes predominant;
due to the predominance of the faculty of concentration, one is a "body-witness."
For one who attends to [phenomena] as non-self, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the faculty of wisdom, one attains right view.
Thinking, "I am liberated through faith,"—
One liberated by faith is "liberated through faith.
One who has touched [the goal] and realized it is "a body-witness."
Because he has seen, he has attained—
thus, one who has attained through vision (diṭṭhippatto). One who has faith is liberated— thus...
One liberated by faith:
first he touches the contact of jhāna, and afterwards he realizes cessation, Nibbāna—
he is a body-witness.
“When it is known, seen, understood, realized, and touched by wisdom that ‘conditioned phenomena are suffering, cessation is bliss’—this is one who has attained vision.

Now, as for this person liberated by faith, this body-witness, and this one who has attained vision: these three types of persons may, according to their basis and by way of alternative description, be each called liberated by faith, a body-witness, or one who has attained vision.”
And how might this be?
For one who attends to [the aggregates] as impermanent, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the faculty of faith, one is "liberated by faith."
When one attends to [the aggregates] as suffering, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the faculty of faith, one is "liberated by faith.
When one attends to them as non-self, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Because the faculty of faith (*saddhindriya*) is predominant, one is "liberated by faith" (*saddhāvimutta*).
Thus, these three types of persons are liberated by faith through the power of the faculty of faith.
When one attends to [the aggregates] as suffering, the faculty of concentration (*samādhindriya*) becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the faculty of concentration, one becomes a body-witness.
For one who attends to [the body] as non-self, the faculty of concentration becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the faculty of concentration, one becomes a body-witness.
For one who attends to the impermanent, the faculty of concentration becomes preeminent.
Due to the preeminence of the faculty of concentration, one becomes a body-witness (*kāyasakkhī*).
Thus, these three types of persons are body-witnesses by way of the faculty of concentration.
For one who attends to [phenomena] as non-self, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the faculty of wisdom, one becomes one who has attained vision.
For one who attends to [phenomena] as impermanent, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
One becomes one who has attained vision through the predominance of the faculty of wisdom.
When one attends to [the aggregates] as suffering, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Through the predominance of the faculty of wisdom, one becomes one who has attained vision.
Thus, these three persons have attained vision by means of the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*).

Furthermore, as for this person who is liberated by faith (*saddhāvimutta*), the body-witness (*kāyasakkhī*), and the one who has attained vision (*diṭṭhippatto*): in this way, these three persons may, according to their respective bases and by way of alternative explanation, be called "liberated by faith," "body-witnesses," and "those who have attained vision.
As for this person who is liberated by faith, the body-witness, and the one who has attained vision: these three persons may... [and so forth].
One liberated by faith is indeed one thing, a body-witness another, and one attained to view yet another.
How might this be so?
When one attends to [phenomena] as impermanent, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the faculty of faith, one is "liberated by faith.
When one attends to them as suffering, the faculty of concentration becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the faculty of concentration, one becomes a body-witness (*kāyasakkhī*).
When attending to [the aggregates] as non-self, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the faculty of wisdom, one becomes one who has attained vision (*diṭṭhippatto*).

As for this person who is liberated by faith, this person who is a body-witness, and this person who has attained vision—it may be that these three persons are, according to their basis and by way of designation, respectively liberated by faith, a body-witness, and one who has attained vision.
Yet the one liberated by faith is indeed distinct, the body-witness is distinct, and the one who has attained vision is distinct.
When one attends to things as impermanent, the faculty of faith becomes predominant; because the faculty of faith is predominant, one attains the path of stream-entry.
Therefore it is said:
"one who follows through faith.
The four faculties follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions.
Through the faculty of faith, there is the development of the four faculties.
For whoever attains the path of stream-entry through the faculty of faith, all such persons are followers by faith (*saddhānusārī*).
When one attends to [the aggregates] as impermanent, the faculty of faith becomes predominant; because the faculty of faith is predominant, the fruit of stream-entry is realized.
Therefore it is said:
"one liberated by faith.
The four faculties follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions.
By means of the faculty of faith (*saddhindriya*), the four faculties are developed and well-developed.
Whosoever has realized the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) by means of the faculty of faith, all of them are "liberated through faith" (*saddhāvimutta*).

When one attends to [the aggregates] as impermanent, the faculty of faith becomes predominant; because the faculty of faith is predominant, one attains the path of the once-returner (*sakadāgāmimagga*) …pe…
The fruit of once-returning is realized …pe… he attains the path of non-returning … the fruit of non-returning is realized …pe…
One attains the path of arahantship … arahantship is realized;
therefore it is said:
“One liberated by faith.
The four faculties follow along with it … [and so on] … they function as associated conditions.
By means of the faculty of faith, the four faculties are developed and well-developed.
Whosoever have realized arahantship by means of the faculty of faith, all of them are "liberated through faith" (saddhāvimutta).

For one who attends to [the aggregates] as suffering, the faculty of concentration becomes predominant; because of the predominance of the faculty of concentration, one attains the path of stream-entry.
Therefore, it is called a "body-witness" (kāyasakkhī).
The four faculties follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions.
Through the power of the faculty of concentration, there is the development of the four faculties.
For whoever attains the path of stream-entry through the power of the faculty of concentration, all of them are body-witnesses (*kāyasakkhī*).
When one attends to things as suffering, the faculty of concentration becomes predominant; because the faculty of concentration is predominant, the fruit of stream-entry is realized …pe…
He attains the path of once-returning …pe… he realizes the fruit of once-returning …pe… he attains the path of non-returning …pe…
The fruit of non-returning is realized …pe… one attains the path of arahantship …pe… the state of arahantship is realized.
Therefore it is said:
"one who is a body-witness.
The four faculties follow along with that; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions.
By means of the faculty of concentration, the four faculties are developed and well-developed.
Indeed, whoever has realized arahantship by means of the faculty of concentration—all such persons are body-witnesses (*kāyasakkhī*).
When one attends to [phenomena] as non-self, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant; because the faculty of wisdom is predominant, one attains the path of stream-entry (*sotāpatti-magga*).
Therefore it is said:
“one who follows through the Dhamma.
The four faculties follow along with that …pe…
They exist as associated conditions.
Through the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*), there is the development of the four faculties.
For whoever attains the path of stream-entry through the faculty of wisdom, all such persons are followers by Dhamma (*dhammānusārino*).
For one who attends to [phenomena] as non-self, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant; because the faculty of wisdom is predominant, the fruit of stream-entry is realized.
Therefore, it is said:
"one who has attained vision."
The four faculties follow along with it … they serve as associated conditions.
By means of the faculty of wisdom, the four faculties are developed and well developed.
For whoever has realized the fruit of stream-entry by means of the faculty of wisdom, all of them are those who have attained through vision (*diṭṭhippatta*).

When one attends to [phenomena] as non-self, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant; because the faculty of wisdom is predominant, one attains the path of the once-returner …pe… the fruit of the once-returner is realized …pe…
He attains the path of non-returning … the fruit of non-returning is realized … he attains the path of arahantship … [and so on] …
Arahatship has been realized;
therefore, one is called "attained to vision."
The four faculties follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions.
By means of the faculty of wisdom, the four faculties are developed and well-developed.
For whoever has realized arahantship by means of the faculty of wisdom, all of them have attained through vision.
For whoever has developed, is developing, or will develop renunciation; has attained, is attaining, or will attain it;
has reached, is reaching, or will reach it; has acquired, is acquiring, or will acquire it;
has penetrated, is penetrating, or will penetrate it; has realized—
Whether they have realized it, will realize it; have touched it, are touching it, or will touch it;
have attained mastery, are attaining it, or will attain it; have attained perfection, are attaining it, or will attain it;
or have attained fearlessness, are attaining it, or will attain it—all of them do so by means of the faculty of faith.
Those liberated by faith, those who are body-witnesses through the faculty of concentration, and those who have attained vision through the faculty of wisdom.
Whosoever [practices] non-ill will …pe… the perception of light …
Non-distraction … discernment of phenomena … knowledge …
Gladness … the first jhāna … the second jhāna …
the third jhāna … the fourth jhāna … the attainment of the base of infinite space …
the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness … the attainment of the base of nothingness … the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …
contemplation of impermanence … contemplation of suffering … contemplation of non-self …
contemplation of disenchantment … contemplation of dispassion … contemplation of cessation …
contemplation of relinquishment … contemplation of destruction … contemplation of vanishing …
contemplation of change … contemplation of the signless … contemplation of the desireless …
contemplation of emptiness … higher wisdom as insight into phenomena … knowledge and vision of things as they truly are …
contemplation of danger … contemplation of reflection … contemplation of turning away …
the path of stream-entry … the path of once-returning … the path of non-returning …
The path to arahantship… For whoever [practices] the four foundations of mindfulness… the four right efforts…
The four bases of psychic power … the five faculties … the five powers …
The seven factors of enlightenment...
the noble eightfold path...
whoever has developed, is developing, or will develop the eight liberations, or has attained, is attaining, or will attain them.
Or they will attain; or have attained, are attaining, or will attain;
or have acquired, are acquiring, or will acquire; or have penetrated, are penetrating, or will penetrate;
or have realized, are realizing, or will realize; or have touched, are touching, or will touch.
Whether they have attained mastery, are attaining it, or will attain it; whether they have attained perfection, are attaining it, or will attain it;
or whether they have attained fearlessness, are attaining it, or will attain it—all of them, by virtue of the faculty of faith, are those liberated through faith (*saddhā-vimutta*);
by virtue of the faculty of concentration, they are body-witnesses (*kāya-sakkhī*); and by virtue of the faculty of wisdom, they are those who have attained vision (*diṭṭhi-ppatta*).

For whoever has attained, is attaining, or will attain the four analytical knowledges (*paṭisambhidā*)—all of them, by virtue of the faculty of faith, are those liberated through faith (*saddhāvimutta*);
by virtue of the faculty of concentration, they are body-witnesses (*kāyasakkhī*); and by virtue of the faculty of wisdom, they are those who have reached vision (*diṭṭhippatto*).
For whoever has penetrated, is penetrating, or will penetrate the three true insights (*tisso vijjā*)—all of them [are likewise].

All of them are liberated by faith through the power of the faculty of faith; they are body-witnesses through the power of the faculty of concentration; and they have attained vision through the power of the faculty of wisdom.
For whoever has trained, is training, or will train in the three trainings; whoever has realized, is realizing, or will realize [the goal]; whoever has touched, is touching, or will touch [the goal];
or whoever has attained, is attaining, or will attain mastery—[all these are included therein].
Whether they have attained, are attaining, or will attain perfection;
whether they have attained, are attaining, or will attain fearlessness—every one of them, by virtue of the faculty of faith, is liberated through faith (*saddhāvimutta*);
by virtue of the faculty of concentration, is a body-witness (*kāyasakkhī*); and by virtue of the faculty of wisdom, has attained vision (*diṭṭhippatta*).
For whoever fully understands suffering, abandons its origin, realizes its cessation, and develops the path—
all of them are liberated by faith through the power of the faculty of faith, body-witnesses through the power of the faculty of concentration,
and those who have attained vision through the power of the faculty of wisdom.
In how many ways is there penetration of the truths? In how many ways does one penetrate the truths?
There is penetration of the truths in four ways.
One penetrates the truths in four ways:
one penetrates the truth of suffering through the penetration of full understanding; one penetrates the truth of the origin through the penetration of abandoning;
one penetrates the truth of cessation through the penetration of realization; and one penetrates the truth of the path through the penetration of development.
The penetration of the truths occurs in these four ways.

Penetrating the truths in these four ways, one is liberated by faith through the influence of the faculty of faith (*saddhindriya*), a body-witness through the influence of the faculty of concentration (*samādhindriya*), and one who has attained vision through the influence of the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*).
In how many ways does the penetration of the truths occur?
In how many ways does one penetrate the truths?
There is penetration of the truths in nine ways; one penetrates the truths in nine ways.
One penetrates the truth of suffering through the penetration of full understanding; one penetrates the truth of the origin through the penetration of abandoning.
One penetrates the truth of cessation through the penetration of realization; one penetrates the truth of the path through the penetration of development.

There is the penetration of direct knowledge regarding all phenomena, the penetration of full understanding regarding all conditioned formations, the penetration of abandonment regarding all unwholesome states, the penetration of development regarding the four paths, and the penetration of realization regarding cessation.
In these nine ways there is penetration of the truths.

Penetrating the truths in these nine ways, one is liberated by faith through the influence of the faculty of faith; a body-witness through the influence of the faculty of concentration; and one who has attained vision through the influence of the faculty of wisdom.
The second recitation section.
When attending to formations as impermanent, how do they appear?
When attending to them as suffering, how do they appear?
When attending to them as non-self, how do they appear?
When one attends to formations as impermanent, they appear as subject to destruction.
When one attends to them as suffering, they appear as fearful.
When one attends to them as non-self, they appear as empty.
When attending to [the object] as impermanent, what is the mind mostly like?
When attending to it as suffering, what is the mind mostly like?
When attending to it as non-self, what is the mind mostly like?
When attending to [the object] as impermanent, the mind becomes abundant in resolve.
When attending to it as suffering, the mind becomes abundant in tranquility.
When attending to it as non-self, the mind becomes abundant in wisdom.
Contemplating as impermanent, one who is abundant in resolution (adhimokkha) attains which liberation?
Contemplating as suffering, one who is abundant in tranquility (passaddhi) attains which liberation?
Contemplating as non-self, one who is abundant in knowledge (ñāṇa) attains which liberation?
One who attends to [phenomena] as impermanent and abounds in resolution attains the signless liberation.
One who attends to them as suffering and abounds in tranquility attains the desireless liberation.
One who attends to them as non-self and abounds in wisdom attains the emptiness liberation.
For one who attends to [the object] as impermanent and is abundant in resolution (*adhimokkha*), what liberation (*vimokkha*) is predominant?

In the development (*bhāvanā*), how many liberations follow upon it; how many are co-nascent conditions (*sahajāta-paccaya*); how many are mutual conditions (*aññamañña-paccaya*); how many are support conditions (*nissaya-paccaya*);
how many are associated conditions (*sampayutta-paccaya*); how many have a single flavor (*ekarasa*)? In what sense is there "development," and who develops?
For one who attends to [the body] as suffering and possesses abundant tranquility, what liberation is predominant?
In the development [of this], how many liberations follow upon it? Are they co-nascent conditions? Are they mutual conditions? Are they support conditions?
Are they associated conditions? Do they have a single flavor? In what sense is there "development"? Who develops it?
For one who attends to [the aggregates] as non-self and is abundant in wisdom, what liberation is predominant?

In the development [of this], how many liberations follow along with it, are co-nascent conditions, are mutual conditions, are support conditions, are associated conditions, and are of a single flavor? In what sense is there "development," and who develops?
For one who attends to the impermanent and is abundant in resolution, the signless liberation is predominant.
Through cultivation, two liberations follow upon it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, associated conditions, and they have a single flavor.
In the sense of having a single flavor, there is cultivation.
One who has practiced rightly develops [this];
for one who has practiced wrongly, there is no development of liberation.
For one who attends to [the body] as suffering and abounds in tranquility, the wishless liberation becomes predominant.
Through cultivation, the two liberations follow upon it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions; they have a single flavor.
In the sense of having a single flavor, there is cultivation.
One who has practiced rightly cultivates.
For one who has entered upon a wrong course, there is no development of liberation.
For one who attends to [phenomena] as non-self and is abundant in wisdom, the liberation through emptiness becomes predominant.

Through that development, the other two liberations follow along with it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, associated conditions, and they possess a single flavor.
Development is in the sense of having a single flavor.
One who is practicing rightly develops it;
for one who is practicing wrongly, there is no development of liberation.
For one who attends to [the object] as impermanent and is predominant in resolution, which liberation is dominant?
At the time of development, how many liberations follow upon it; how many are co-nascent conditions; how many are mutual conditions; how many are support conditions;
how many are associated conditions; and how many have a single flavor? At the time of penetration, which liberation is dominant?
How many liberations are there that follow upon penetration? How are they related as co-nascent conditions, as mutual conditions, as support conditions, and as associated conditions?
How do they have a single flavor? In what sense is there "development" (bhāvanā), and in what sense is there "penetration" (paṭivedha)?
For one who attends to [the body] as suffering and abounds in tranquility, which liberation is predominant?
At the time of development, how many liberations follow upon it; how many are co-nascent conditions; how many are mutual conditions; how many are support conditions;
how many are associated conditions; and how many have a single flavor? At the time of penetration, which liberation is predominant?

How many liberations (vimokkha) follow upon that penetration (paṭivedha)? Are they co-nascent conditions (sahajāta-paccaya), mutual conditions (aññamañña-paccaya), support conditions (nissaya-paccaya), or associated conditions (sampayutta-paccaya)?
Are they of a single flavor (ekarasa)? In what sense is there "development" (bhāvanā), and in what sense is there "penetration" (paṭivedha)?
For one who attends to [the aggregates] as non-self and is abundant in wisdom, which liberation is predominant?

At the time of development, how many liberations follow upon that, are co-nascent conditions, are mutual conditions, are support conditions, are associated conditions, and are of a single flavor? At the time of penetration, which liberation is predominant?
There is [this]. For the sake of penetration, how many liberations are its concomitants? Are they co-nascent conditions?
Are they mutual conditions? Are they support conditions? Are they associated conditions? Are they of a single flavor? In what sense is there "development" (bhāvanā)?
In what sense is there "penetration" (paṭivedha)?
For one who attends to [the object] as impermanent and is abundant in resolution, the signless liberation is predominant.
Through cultivation, two liberations follow upon it: they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions;
they have a single flavor. At the time of penetration as well, there is the signless liberation.

He becomes dominant; for the sake of penetration, the two liberations follow upon it, being co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions; they have a single flavor.

In the sense of having a single flavor, there is development (*bhāvanā*); in the sense of seeing, there is penetration (*paṭivedha*). Thus, while penetrating, one develops; while developing, one penetrates.
For one who attends to [the body] as suffering and possesses great tranquility, the wishless liberation is predominant;
through cultivation, two liberations follow it, being co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, associated conditions, and of a single flavor;
and at the time of penetration as well, there is the wishless liberation.
He becomes dominant; for the sake of penetration, two liberations follow upon it, acting as co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions;

they have a single flavor, and in the sense of having a single flavor, there is development (*bhāvanā*); in the sense of seeing, there is penetration (*paṭivedha*). Thus, while penetrating, one develops; while developing, one penetrates.
For one who attends to [the aggregates] as non-self and is abundant in wisdom, the liberation through emptiness is predominant.
Through that meditation, two liberations follow it: they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions;
they have a single flavor. At the time of penetration as well, the liberation through emptiness is predominant.
For the sake of penetration, the two liberations follow upon it; they are co-nascent conditions, mutual conditions, support conditions, and associated conditions;
they have a single flavor. In the sense of having a single flavor, there is development (*bhāvanā*);
in the sense of seeing, there is penetration (*paṭivedha*). Thus, while penetrating, one develops; while developing, one penetrates.
When attending to [the object] as impermanent, which liberation becomes predominant?
Through the predominance of which liberation does one become "liberated by faith"?
When attending to [the object] as suffering, which liberation becomes predominant?
Through the predominance of which liberation does one become a body-witness (*kāyasakkhī*)?
When attending to [phenomena] as non-self, which liberation becomes predominant?
Through the predominance of which liberation does one become one who has attained vision (*diṭṭhippatto*)?
For one who attends to [the object] as impermanent, the signless liberation becomes predominant.
Due to the predominance of the signless liberation, one is liberated by faith.
For one who attends to [the object] as suffering, the desireless liberation becomes predominant.
Due to the preponderance of the wishless liberation, one becomes a body-witness.
For one who attends to things as non-self, the void liberation becomes preponderant.
Due to the preponderance of the void liberation, one becomes one who has attained vision.
One who is liberated by means of faith is "liberated through faith" (saddhāvimutta).
One who has realized [the truth] because of having touched it is...
A body-witness.
One who has attained through seeing is thus called "one who has attained through vision" (diṭṭhippatto).
One who is liberated by believing is "liberated-by-faith" (saddhā-vimutto).
One who first touches the contact of jhāna and subsequently realizes cessation, Nibbāna, is [one liberated by insight].
A body-witness. “Formations are suffering, cessation is bliss”— this has been understood, seen, known, realized, and touched by means of wisdom—
thus he is one who has attained vision …pe… [as before].
For whoever has developed, is developing, or will develop renunciation … all of them, by way of the signless liberation, are liberated through faith;
by way of the desireless liberation, they are body-witnesses; by way of the void liberation, they have attained vision.
For whoever [has developed] non-ill will … [the same applies].
the perception of light...
non-distraction...
for whoever fully understands suffering, abandons its origin, realizes its cessation, and [develops] the path...
All those who develop [these liberations] are, by way of the signless liberation, liberated through faith;
by way of the desireless liberation, they are body-witnesses; and by way of the emptiness liberation, they have attained vision.
In how many aspects does the penetration of the truths occur?
In how many ways does one penetrate the truths?
There is penetration of the truths in four ways; one penetrates the truths in four ways.
One penetrates the truth of suffering through the penetration of full understanding; one penetrates the truth of the origin through the penetration of abandoning;
one penetrates the truth of cessation through the penetration of realization;
one penetrates the truth of the path through the penetration of development.
The penetration of the truths occurs in these four ways.

Penetrating the truths in these four ways, one is liberated by faith through the gateway of the signless liberation, a body-witness through the gateway of the desireless liberation, and one who has attained vision through the gateway of the emptiness liberation.
In how many ways does the penetration of the truths occur?
In how many ways does one penetrate the truths?
There is penetration of the truths in nine ways. One penetrates the truths in nine ways.
One penetrates the penetration by full understanding of the truth of suffering … [and so on] … and there is the penetration by realization of cessation.
In these nine ways there is the penetration of the truths.

Piercing through to the truths by these nine modes, one is "liberated by faith" by way of the signless liberation (*animitta-vimokkha*), a "body-witness" (*kāyasakkhī*) by way of the desireless liberation (*appaṇihita-vimokkha*), and "attained to vision" (*diṭṭhippatto*) by way of the emptiness liberation (*suññata-vimokkha*).
When attending to things as impermanent, what phenomena does one know and see as they truly are?
How does right seeing come about?
How, by following that sequence, are all conditioned phenomena clearly seen as impermanent?
Wherein is doubt abandoned?
When attending to them as suffering, what phenomena does one know and see as they really are?
How does right view arise?
How, following from that, are all conditioned phenomena clearly seen as suffering?
Wherein is doubt abandoned?
When attending to [phenomena] as non-self, what phenomena does one know and see as they really are?
How does right vision come about?
And how, by following that, are all phenomena clearly seen as non-self?
Wherein is doubt abandoned?
One who attends to [the object] as impermanent knows and sees the sign as it really is;
therefore it is said:
“Right seeing.
Thus, by following that sequence, all conditioned phenomena are clearly seen as impermanent.
Herein, doubt is abandoned.
When attending to it as suffering, one knows and sees the process of existence as it truly is;
therefore, it is called "right vision."
In this way, by means of that sequence, all conditioned phenomena are clearly seen as suffering.
Herein, doubt is abandoned.
When attending to them as non-self, one knows and sees both the sign and the occurrence as they truly are.
Therefore it is said:
"right seeing.
In this way, by following that [insight], all phenomena are clearly seen as non-self.
Herein, doubt is abandoned.
