Now, as to that which is knowledge of things as they really are, that which is right vision, and that which is the overcoming of doubt: are these states different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they one in meaning and different only in phrasing?
That which is knowledge of things as they really are, that which is right vision, and that which is the overcoming of doubt: these states are one in meaning, and different only in phrasing.
When one attends to [the aggregates] as impermanent, what appears as a danger?
When one attends to them as suffering, what appears as a danger?
When one attends to them as non-self, what appears as a danger?
When one attends to [the object] as impermanent, the sign appears as fear.
When one attends to it as suffering, the occurrence appears as fear.
When one attends to it as non-self, both the sign and the occurrence appear as fear.

Is the wisdom that arises from the appearance of fear, the knowledge of danger, and disenchantment—these states different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they one in meaning with only the phrasing being different?
The wisdom that arises from the appearance of fear, the knowledge of danger, and disenchantment—these states are one in meaning; only the phrasing is different.
Is the contemplation of non-self and the contemplation of emptiness—these states different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they one in meaning with only the phrasing being different?
The contemplation of non-self and the contemplation of emptiness: these states have the same meaning; only the phrasing is different.
When one attends to things as impermanent, what kind of reflective knowledge arises?
When one attends to things as suffering, what kind of reflective knowledge arises?
When one attends to [phenomena] as non-self, what kind of reflective knowledge arises?
When one attends to them as impermanent, reflective knowledge of the sign arises.
When one attends to them as suffering, reflective knowledge of occurrence arises.
When one attends to [the aggregates] as non-self, there arises the knowledge of reflective contemplation regarding both the sign and the occurrence.

Now, as for the desire for deliverance, the contemplation of reflection, and equanimity toward formations—do these states have different meanings and different expressions, or do they have the same meaning and differ only in expression?
The desire for deliverance, the contemplation of reflection, and equanimity toward formations: these states have the same meaning; they differ only in expression.
When one attends to things as impermanent, from what does the mind emerge, and where does the mind leap forward?
When one attends to things as suffering, from what does the mind emerge, and where does the mind leap forward?
When one attends to things as non-self, from what does the mind emerge, and where does the mind leap forward?
When one attends to [phenomena] as impermanent, the mind emerges from signs and leaps into the signless.
When one attends to them as suffering, the mind emerges from occurrence and leaps into non-occurrence.
When one attends to them as non-self, the mind emerges from both signs and occurrence, and leaps into the cessation that is signless, non-occurring, and the element of Nibbāna.

The wisdom regarding emergence and turning away from the external, and the states of the lineage-change (gotrabhū)—are these states different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they identical in meaning and only different in phrasing?
The wisdom regarding emergence and turning away from the external and the states of the lineage-change—these states are identical in meaning; only the phrasing is different.
When one attends to [the external] as impermanent, by which liberation is one liberated?
When attending to [the object] as suffering, by which liberation is one liberated?
When attending to it as non-self, by which liberation is one liberated?
When attending to it as impermanent, one is liberated by the signless liberation (*animitta-vimokkha*).
One who attends to [the aggregates] as suffering is liberated by the liberation of the wishless.
One who attends to them as non-self is liberated by the liberation of the void.

Now, regarding the wisdom that emerges from both and turns away [from them], and the knowledge of the path: are these states different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they identical in meaning and only different in phrasing?
The wisdom regarding emergence and turning away from both, and the knowledge of the path—these states are identical in meaning; only the phrasing is different.
In how many ways do the three liberations occur at different moments?
In how many ways do the three liberations occur at the same moment?
The three liberations occur at different moments in four ways;
they occur in a single moment in seven ways.
In which four ways do the three liberations occur at different moments?
In the sense of predominance, in the sense of resolution, in the sense of directing, and in the sense of outlet.
How are the three liberations predominant in the sense of predominance at different times?

For one who attends to the impermanent, the signless liberation is predominant; for one who attends to the painful, the desireless liberation is predominant; for one who attends to the not-self, the void liberation is predominant.
Thus, in the sense of predominance, the three liberations occur at different times.
How do the three liberations occur at different times in the sense of resolution?
One who attends to [the object] as impermanent resolves the mind by means of the signless liberation; one who attends to it as suffering...
By means of the wishless liberation, one resolves the mind; by means of the emptiness liberation, one resolves the mind while attending to [phenomena] as non-self.
Thus, in the sense of resolution, the three liberations occur at different moments.
In what sense do the three liberations exist at different times in the sense of directing the mind?
One who attends to [the object] as impermanent directs the mind by way of the signless liberation; one who attends to it as suffering directs the mind by way of the desireless liberation;
one who attends to it as non-self directs the mind by way of the emptiness liberation.
By means of this, one directs the mind.
Thus, in the sense of directing, the three liberations occur at different times.
How do the three liberations occur at different times in the sense of deliverance?
One who attends to [the aggregates] as impermanent leads to Nibbāna, which is cessation, by way of the signless liberation;

one who attends to them as suffering leads to Nibbāna, which is cessation, by way of the desireless liberation; one who attends to them as non-self leads to Nibbāna, which is cessation, by way of the emptiness liberation.
Thus, in the sense of leading out, the three liberations occur at different times.
In these four ways, the three liberations occur at different times.
In which seven ways do the three liberations occur at one and the same time?

In the sense of convergence, in the sense of attainment, in the sense of acquisition, in the sense of penetration, in the sense of realization, in the sense of touching, and in the sense of clear comprehension.

How, in the sense of convergence, in the sense of attainment, in the sense of acquisition, in the sense of penetration, in the sense of realization, in the sense of touching, and in the sense of clear comprehension, are the three liberations present in a single moment?
When one attends to [the object] as impermanent, one is released from the sign. Thus...
The signless liberation.
That from which one is liberated, therein one does not form a wish—
this is the wishless liberation.
Wherein one does not aspire—that is empty; thus it is the emptiness liberation.
That by which it is empty, by that sign it is signless—thus it is the signless liberation.
The signless liberation.

Thus, in the sense of convergence, in the sense of attainment, in the sense of acquisition, in the sense of penetration, in the sense of realization, in the sense of contact, and in the sense of clear comprehension, the three liberations occur simultaneously.
One who attends to [the object] as suffering is liberated from longing.
The wishless liberation.
That wherein one does not form a wish is empty of that—
this is the emptiness liberation.
That by which it is empty, by that sign it is signless—
this is the signless liberation.
That by which it is signless, therein one does not form an aspiration— this is the wishless liberation.
the wishless liberation.

Thus, in the sense of convergence, in the sense of attainment, in the sense of acquisition, in the sense of penetration, in the sense of realization, in the sense of touching, and in the sense of clear comprehension, the three liberations occur in a single moment.
One who attends to [phenomena] as non-self is liberated from misapprehension.
The void liberation.
That which is signless by virtue of that by which it is void—
this is the signless liberation.
Because it is signless by means of whatever sign [there might be], one does not long for that—
this is the signless liberation.
Because one does not long for that wherein there is nothing to long for, it is empty— this is the emptiness liberation.
The void liberation.

Thus, in the sense of convergence, in the sense of attainment, in the sense of acquisition, in the sense of penetration, in the sense of realization, in the sense of contact, and in the sense of clear comprehension, the three liberations occur simultaneously.
In these seven ways, the three liberations occur at one and the same moment.

There is liberation; there is the door; there is the gateway to liberation; there is what is contrary to liberation; there is what is in conformity with liberation; there is the turning away from liberation; there is the development of liberation; there is the subsiding of liberation. What is liberation?
The void liberation, the signless liberation, and the desireless liberation.
What is the void liberation?
The knowledge of contemplation of impermanence is liberated from misapprehension as permanent;
thus it is the void liberation.
The knowledge of contemplation of suffering is liberated from the misapprehension of it as pleasant;
thus it is the void liberation.
The knowledge of contemplation of non-self is liberated from the misapprehension of it as self; thus...
The void liberation:
the knowledge of contemplation of disenchantment is liberated from attachment to delight;
thus it is the void liberation.
The knowledge of contemplation of dispassion is the void liberation because it is liberated from the misapprehension of lust.
The knowledge of contemplation of cessation is the void liberation because it is liberated from the misapprehension of origination.
The void liberation:
the knowledge of contemplation of relinquishment is liberated from grasping and adherence;
thus it is the void liberation.
The knowledge of contemplation of the signless is the void liberation because it is liberated from misinterpreting by way of signs.
The knowledge of contemplation of the desireless is [the void liberation] because it is liberated from misinterpreting by way of desire.
The void liberation:
the knowledge of contemplation of voidness is liberated from all forms of misapprehension;
thus it is the void liberation.
Knowledge of contemplation of impermanence in material form is liberated from misinterpreting it as permanent:
this is the void liberation. … Knowledge of contemplation of voidness in material form is liberated from all misinterpretations: this is the void liberation. …pe…
The void liberation.

Knowledge of contemplation of impermanence is liberated from the sign of permanence;

The signless liberation.

What is the door?
Those blameless, wholesome states conducive to enlightenment that arise therein—this is the door.
What is the door to liberation?
That which is the object of those phenomena—cessation, Nibbāna—is the door to liberation.
It is called the "door to liberation" because it is both liberation and a door; this is the door to liberation.
What is the opposite of liberation?

The three unwholesome roots are opposites of liberation; the three types of misconduct are opposites of liberation; all unwholesome states are opposites of liberation—this is the opposite of liberation.
What is in conformity with liberation?

The three roots of skillfulness are in conformity with liberation; the three types of good conduct are in conformity with liberation; all wholesome states (*dhamma*) are also in conformity with liberation—this is conformity with liberation.
What is turning away from liberation?
Turning away through perception, turning away through mind, turning away through consciousness, turning away through knowledge, turning away through liberation, and turning away through truth.

"One turns away by means of knowledge"— thus it is the turning away through knowledge (*ñāṇavivaṭṭa*).

It is the turning away through liberation.
It turns away in the sense of suchness— thus it is the turning away of the truths.
Where there is the turning away from perception, there is the turning away of the mind; where there is the turning away of the mind, there is the turning away from perception.

Where there is the turning away from perception and the turning away of the mind, there is the turning away of consciousness; where there is the turning away of consciousness, there is the turning away from perception and the turning away of the mind.

Where there is the turning away from perception, the turning away of the mind, and the turning away of consciousness, there is the turning away through knowledge; where there is the turning away through knowledge, there is the turning away from perception, the turning away of the mind, and the turning away of consciousness.

Where there is the turning away from perception, the turning away of the mind, the turning away of consciousness, and the turning away of knowledge, there is the turning away through liberation; where there is the turning away through liberation, there is the turning away from perception, the turning away of the mind, the turning away of consciousness, and the turning away of knowledge.

Where there is the turning away from perception, the turning away of the mind, the turning away of consciousness, the turning away of knowledge, and the turning away through liberation, there is the turning away from the truths;

where there is the turning away from the truths, there is the turning away from perception, the turning away of the mind, the turning away of consciousness, the turning away of knowledge, and the turning away through liberation.
This is the turning away through liberation.
